ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a resistor network circuit. On the left there is an ideal 1 V voltage source, marked with the upper end positive and the lower end negative. The bottom is a common wire serving as the lower node. The upper-left node connects several branches: inside on the left there are two 1 Ω resistors in series connected to the bottom, and in the center there is a 2 Ω resistor connected to the bottom; from the upper-left node, through a top 1 Ω resistor, it connects to the upper-right node. From the upper-right node downward there are two parallel vertical 2 Ω resistors connected to the bottom, and beside the rightmost 2 Ω resistor a downward current I is marked. Reasoning: According to the method stated in the problem, take the bottom common node as the reference ground 0 V. Since the upper end of the ideal 1 V voltage source on the left is positive, the voltage of the upper-left node is +1 V. For calculating the voltage of the upper-right node, the left-side branches directly connected in parallel across the two ends of the source do not change the fixed 1 V node voltage of the ideal source, and may be ignored. The two 2 Ω resistors on the right are in parallel, with equivalent resistance 2 Ω || 2 Ω = 1 Ω. This 1 Ω equivalent resistance is supplied from the 1 V node through the top 1 Ω resistor, therefore forming a voltage divider of 1 Ω and 1 Ω, and the upper-right node voltage is 1 V × 1/(1+1) = 0.5 V. The voltage across the rightmost 2 Ω resistor marked with the current is 0.5 V, so I = 0.5 V / 2 Ω = 0.25 A, in the downward direction.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure, then solve: treat the bottom rail as reference and the left top node as +1 V because of the ideal 1 V source. Ignore the other branches directly across the source for the right-node voltage calculation. Combine the two right-side 2 Ω resistors in parallel to get 1 Ω. This 1 Ω equivalent is fed through the top 1 Ω resistor from the 1 V node, so use a 1 Ω–1 Ω voltage divider to get the right top node voltage as 0.5 V. The current through the labeled far-right 2 Ω resistor is then I = 0.5 V / 2 Ω = 0.25 A downward.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个电阻网络电路，左侧有一个理想 1 V 电压源，标注上端为正、下端为负。底部是一条公共导线作为下端节点。左上节点连接若干支路：左侧内部有两个 1 Ω 电阻串联接到底部，中央有一个 2 Ω 电阻接到底部；从左上节点经过顶部一个 1 Ω 电阻连接到右上节点。右上节点向下有两个并联的 2 Ω 竖直电阻接到底部，其中最右侧 2 Ω 电阻旁标出了向下的电流 I。
推理：按题设方法，将底部公共节点作为参考地 0 V。由于左侧理想 1 V 电压源上端为正，左上节点电压为 +1 V。对于右上节点电压计算，直接并联在电源两端的左侧支路不改变理想电源固定的 1 V 节点电压，可忽略。右侧两个 2 Ω 电阻并联，等效电阻为 2 Ω || 2 Ω = 1 Ω。该 1 Ω 等效电阻通过顶部 1 Ω 电阻由 1 V 节点供电，因此形成 1 Ω 与 1 Ω 的分压，右上节点电压为 1 V × 1/(1+1) = 0.5 V。最右侧标注电流的 2 Ω 电阻两端电压为 0.5 V，所以 I = 0.5 V / 2 Ω = 0.25 A，方向向下。
